name: Chronic Mast Cell Leukemia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Diagnostic Criteria for Mast Cell Leukemia

criteria.description: Bone marrow infiltration by atypical mast cells exceeding 20% of nucleated cells
Presence of immature or atypical mast cells with abnormal morphology in bone marrow and peripheral blood
Detection of KIT D816V mutation or other activating KIT mutations
Absence of features consistent with acute mast cell leukemia (blast crisis) such as >20% circulating blasts

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Major criterion plus at least one minor criterion; persistent mast cell leukemia with less than 20% circulating mast cells and absence of acute leukemia features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Chronic mast cell leukemia is distinguished from acute mast cell leukemia by lower circulating mast cell counts and more indolent clinical course.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent peripheral blood mastocytosis with atypical mast cells
searchTerms: high mast cell count in blood

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bone marrow infiltration by abnormal mast cells
searchTerms: abnormal mast cells in bone marrow
bone marrow filled with mast cells

common.symptomName: Recurrent episodes of flushing due to mast cell mediator release
Anaphylactoid reactions triggered by physical or chemical stimuli
searchTerms: severe reactions to physical or chemical stimuli

occasional.symptomName: Gastrointestinal cramping and diarrhea due to mast cell mediator effects
Bone pain related to marrow infiltration
searchTerms: aching bones due to marrow involvement
mildly low red cells and platelets

occasional.symptomName: Mild hepatopathy with elevated liver enzymes

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms including headaches and cognitive dysfunction

laboratory: Elevated serum tryptase levels persistently above 20 ng/mL
Peripheral blood smear showing atypical mast cells
Bone marrow biopsy demonstrating dense mast cell infiltration
imaging: Skeletal survey or MRI showing osteolytic lesions or marrow infiltration
other: Flow cytometry showing aberrant mast cell immunophenotype (CD25+, CD2+)
Elevated histamine and prostaglandin metabolites in urine

distinguishingFeatures: Higher percentage (>20%) of circulating mast cells
More aggressive clinical course with rapid progression
Lower mast cell burden in blood
Variable organ involvement without leukemic features
Often indolent or smoldering clinical course

redFlags: Rapid increase in circulating mast cells
Severe anaphylactic episodes refractory to treatment
references: Valent P, Akin C, Hartmann K, et al. Mast cell leukemia: 2021 update on diagnosis, risk stratification, and management. Leukemia. 2021;35(7):1955-1968.
